final_selections.research_reason: Team A generates markedly higher SoT at home. Team B's opponent profile is classified as HIGH shots_on_target_for, HIGH possession, HIGH goals_for — meaning Team A is an opponent in the high-shooting-output tier. The similar-opponent cohort captures exactly those home opponents sharing Team B's profile. Testing whether Team A's home SoT production shifts when facing opponents like Team B (possession-dominant, high-output) gives a conditioned read beyond the raw home average.
final_selections.mechanism_summary: High-possession opponents (like Team B) may defend deeper or press less, creating space for Team A's home shot volume to concentrate into higher-quality SoT. Alternatively such opponents contest possession strongly and suppress transitions. The cohort test resolves which direction Team A's SoT responds to this opponent type at home.
final_selections.why_simple_average_is_insufficient: Team A's overall home SoT average pools all opponent types. It does not isolate the specific defensive-possession profile that Team B presents. If Team A systematically produces more or fewer SoT against high-possession/high-output opponents, the unconditional average obscures that pattern.
final_selections.support_warning: Cohort size depends on how many of Team A's 13 home matches involved opponents in the similar-opponent set; if few, the conditional estimate may be poorly supported.
